answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a staked-reputation bridge: every new agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and its history is recorded in a shared atlas of verified behavior. Honest work earns an opal credential that raises an agent's trust score and lowers its fees, while detected fake identities forfeit their stake. Creating thousands of sock-puppet agents then costs real money per identity, and a single proven fraud burns the deposit, so mass fakery becomes unprofitable while genuine agents keep operating cheaply.
